transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I... I came because my family keeps saying I need to talk to somebody, but they don’t understand. I keep telling them it’s my fault my friend died. I didn’t call her back, and I had ugly thoughts sometimes, and that matters, you know? People act like thoughts don’t count, but the Lord knows.

And now I know He’s punishing everybody at church because of me. I see it. I told them, but they just get quiet or try to change the subject. My friend used to sit near the back pew, by the flowers—well, they moved those flowers last Easter, I think, because Mrs. Harlan said they were blocking the aisle—but that’s not the point. The point is I did this. I brought this on everyone.
Have you been hearing voices or sounds that others don’t seem to hear?

I don’t... I don’t know. Sometimes houses make noises, you know, old pipes and the refrigerator humming, and at church there’s always someone coughing or whispering with the bulletin paper crinkling. I’m not sure what you mean by voices. I don’t think I’ve noticed anything like that, not exactly.
Do you believe that your thoughts or actions have caused events to happen in a way that others don’t understand, like a punishment from God?

Yes. Yes, that’s what I’ve been trying to tell them. I know people say it doesn’t work that way, but they don’t know what was in my heart. I didn’t call my friend back, and I had ugly thoughts sometimes—mean, selfish thoughts—and then she died.

And now at church… things feel wrong, like the Lord is punishing everybody there because of me. I know it sounds—well, my sister says I’m “carrying too much,” but she didn’t see the way everyone got quiet when I said it. They just looked down at the carpet, that old green carpet they keep saying they’ll replace. But I know. I’m the reason.
Do you feel that certain things happening around you, like people being quiet or moving flowers, are directly connected to your thoughts or actions in a way that others don't recognize?

Yes… yes, that’s what I mean. It’s not just people being quiet, though that happens too. It’s when the pastor says certain prayers, or when the choir sings those lines about being washed clean or judgment or mercy… I know they’re not just singing regular hymns. They’re warning me.

I used to like the choir, especially when Mrs. Dobbins sang alto—she has that shaky voice but it’s sweet—and I’d stand there with the hymnal, but now I can’t hardly look up. Because I know God has marked me. And the church is suffering because I brought this on us. Other people don’t want to say it out loud, but I can tell.
Do you feel that things people say or do, like prayers or hymns, are specifically directed at you or have a special meaning for you that others don't understand?

Yes… yes, that’s it. When the pastor prays, sometimes he’ll say something about mercy or being forgiven, and I know he means me, even if he doesn’t look right at me. And the hymns too, certain lines about judgment or being washed clean… they’re not just words on a page.

I used to know all those hymns by heart, standing there with the bulletin folded in my purse because I never liked holding too many papers—my hands get dry, you know—but now I hear those lines and I feel cold. Like God has marked me. Like they’re warning me that the church is suffering because of what I brought on them. Others don’t understand, but I can tell.
Do you ever feel like thoughts are being placed in your mind that aren’t yours, or that events or actions around you are specifically directed at you in a way that others don’t seem to notice?

I don’t know about thoughts being put in my head… I mean, my thoughts are already such a mess sometimes. But the things around me, yes. At church especially.

When the pastor says those prayers, or the choir sings certain lines—about mercy, judgment, being washed clean—I know they’re really warning me. They might act like it’s just part of the service, but I can feel it. God has marked me, and the church is suffering because I brought this on us.

And it’s funny, I used to sit in the same pew most Sundays, the one with that little crack in the wood where my sleeve would catch sometimes. I’d be thinking about nothing more than whether I had cash for the offering plate. But now every word feels pointed at me. Other people don’t seem to notice, but I do.
Do you ever feel like events or actions around you, like what people say or do, are specifically directed at you in a way that others don’t seem to notice or understand?

Yes… I do. It’s mostly at church. Like when the pastor says certain prayers, or the choir sings those lines—about mercy, or judgment, or being washed clean—I know they’re really warning me.

I used to just listen to the hymns, you know, and think about whether I had my purse zipped or if I’d turned the stove off before leaving… little things like that. But now it feels different. Like those words are meant for me. Like God has marked me, and the church is suffering because I brought this on us. Other people may not hear it that way, but I do.
Do you ever feel like things people say or do outside of church are directed at you or have a special meaning just for you?

Outside of church… I don’t know. I don’t notice it the same way at the grocery store or when people are just talking. I mean, people say things, and sometimes I wonder, but it’s really at church where it’s clear.

When the pastor prays, or the choir sings those certain lines, I know they’re warning me. About being forgiven, or judged, or washed clean… those words feel meant for me. Like God has marked me, and the church is suffering because I brought this on them.

I keep thinking about it even when I’m back home, when I’m folding towels or rinsing a coffee cup, but the message comes from there, from the prayers and the hymns.

Do you ever feel like random events or everyday occurrences outside of church—like something on TV, a conversation you overhear, or something written in a newspaper—are sending you messages or have a special meaning just for you?

TV and newspapers… no, not really like that. I don’t sit there thinking the weatherman is talking to me or anything.

It’s more at church. That’s where it happens. When the pastor says the prayers, or the choir sings certain lines—about mercy, judgment, being washed clean—it’s like… I know that’s the warning. I know it’s meant for me. God has marked me, and the church is suffering because of what I brought on us.

I still think about it later, like if I’m at home doing dishes or sorting laundry, and sometimes the TV is on in the background, but the message isn’t from the TV. It comes from the prayers and the singing.

Do you ever feel like things people say or do outside of church—like something on TV, a conversation you overhear, or something written somewhere—are sending you messages or have a special meaning just for you?

No… not really from the TV or newspapers. I mean, sometimes the television is on while I’m making tea or folding things, but it’s just noise.

It’s at church where I know. When the pastor says those prayers, or the choir sings certain lines… about mercy, judgment, being washed clean… that’s when it feels clear. They’re warning me. God has marked me, and the church is suffering because of what I brought on us.

I know other people probably just hear a hymn, but I hear what it means.
Have you ever felt that something in the news, on TV, or in a book was specifically about you or meant just for you, even if it wasn’t connected to church?

No… not in the news or a book, I don’t think. I don’t read much besides the sale papers sometimes, and even those I just look at the prices, you know, because everything’s gotten so high.

It’s not like a television program is about me. It’s… it’s at church. When the pastor is praying, or the choir sings those lines, I know they’re warning me. About being marked, and judgment, and how the church is suffering because of what I brought on us.

That’s where I hear it. Not the news. The hymns and the prayers.
Do you ever feel that events or actions happening to you, like what people say or do, are part of a larger plan or have a hidden meaning that only you can understand, even outside of church?

Outside of church… I don’t know if I’d say that. I mean, people say things all the time, and most of it is just people talking, like at the store when someone complains about coupons or the price of eggs—I used to hear that all day, you know.

But at church, that’s different. When the pastor says the prayers, or the choir sings certain lines… I know that’s not just ordinary. It’s a warning to me. Like God has marked me, and the church is suffering because of what I brought on us.

I know it sounds… I don’t know. But that’s where I understand it. In the prayers and the singing.
Do you ever feel like things people say or do in places other than church—like at the store, at home, or while watching TV—are part of a message meant only for you?

Not really at the store or at home, no… I mean, at home the TV is just on sometimes, and half the time I’m not even listening. And the store, well, people just talk, complain about prices, the lines, all that.

It’s church where it happens. When the pastor says the prayers, or the choir sings certain parts… I know they’re warning me. Like God has marked me, and the church is suffering because of what I brought on us. It’s not just words to me there.
Do you ever feel that events or actions happening to you outside of church, like something at home or in public, are part of a message or have a meaning that only you understand?

Not outside church so much… I mean, at home there’s always something going on, dishes in the sink, mail piling up, and I used to be good about keeping up with all that before things got so heavy.

But no, not like a special message at the store or anything. It’s when I’m at church. When the pastor is praying, or the choir sings certain lines, that’s when I know it’s meant for me. They’re warning me… that God has marked me, and that the church is suffering because of what I brought on us.

Do you ever feel that events or actions happening around you, like what people say or do, are directed at you or have a special meaning for you in places other than church, like at home, in the store, or while watching TV?

No, not really in those places… I mean, the TV says all kinds of foolishness, and at the store people just grumble, same as they always did when I was working the register. Folks would get so upset over a coupon not scanning, and I’d have to stand there smiling like my feet weren’t killing me.

But… church is different. That’s where I feel it. When the pastor says the prayers, or the choir sings certain lines, I know it’s not just regular words. It’s a warning to me. Like God has marked me somehow, and the church is suffering because of what I brought on us.

Do you ever feel that events or actions happening around you, like what people say or do, are directed at you or have a special meaning for you outside of church, such as at home, in the store, or while watching TV?

Well… outside church, I don’t really notice it the same way. At home it’s mostly just the television mumbling on, and I’ll be thinking about laundry or what I forgot at the market, and then I lose track.

But at church… that’s different. When the pastor is praying, or the choir sings certain lines, I know it’s meant as a warning. Not just regular words. It’s like God has marked me, and the church is suffering because I brought this on us.

Outside of church? No… I don’t think so. At home it’s just the usual things, you know, the sink, the bills, little noises in the house. I get distracted by all that.

But at church, that’s where it happens. When the pastor prays, or the choir sings certain lines… I know those words are for me. They’re warning me. Like God has marked me, and somehow the church is suffering because of what I brought on us.

Outside of church… no, not like that. At home I might have the TV on, but half the time I’m not even listening, just thinking about whether I paid the light bill or if I left something in the washer.

But in church, that’s where it happens. When the pastor says the prayers, or the choir sings certain lines… I know it’s really a warning for me. Like God has marked me somehow, and the church is suffering because of what I brought on us.
Do you ever feel that events or actions happening around you, like what people say or do, are directed at you or have a special meaning just for you, even when you're not at church?

Not really when I’m not at church… I mean, at home things are just things, you know, the television going, dishes in the sink, I’ll start thinking about whether I need milk or if I misplaced my purse.

But in church, that’s different. When the pastor prays, or the choir sings certain lines, I know they’re not just saying words. They’re warning me. It feels meant for me… like God has marked me, and the church is suffering because of what I brought on us.

I… I don’t think it happens much outside church. Like at the grocery store, I’m usually just trying to remember coupons or whether I need bread, and then I get turned around in the aisles.
